title: Etale presentation diagrams and the presentation property of a space morphism
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme]. For presheaves of sets $F,G$ on schemes over $S$ and a natural transformation $f:F\to G$, an etale presentation diagram consists of $S$-schemes $U,V$, maps $a:h_U\to F$, $b:h_V\to G$ which are representable etale in the scheme-test sense of [def-trf-algebraic-space], and an $S$-morphism $h:U\to V$ such that $f\circ a=b\circ h_{h}$, where $h_T$ denotes the Yoneda presheaf and $h_h:h_U\to h_V$ is induced by $h$. Scheme etaleness means [def-weil-etale-morphism]. For any property $P$ of scheme morphisms, define the presentation property of $f$ to mean that there exists such a diagram with $a$ representable surjective in the same scheme-test sense and $P(h)$. No surjectivity condition is imposed on $b$. This definition applies in particular to maps between the underlying presheaves of algebraic spaces over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space]; when $P$ is etale local on source and target it is the property of space morphisms defined by etale presentations.
